name: Canvas for AI
description: These tools let agents show work in a canvas for the user.

tools.name: UI Design Editor
tools.summary: People and agents can edit designs together.
use_when: Make an editable page or app mockup.
not_for: Build and host a working website.
Play text or documents as audio.

access.auth: You do not need an account. A Space or project link gives access to the shared work.
requirements: A browser that exposes the page's WebMCP site tools to the agent.
The full Space or project URL when opening existing work.

limits: Anyone with a Space link can edit every project in that Space.
Keep the full #space and &project values in links.
Agent edits need browser site tools.
tools.example_prompt:
Open https://uidesigneditor.com/.
Read https://uidesigneditor.com/instructions.txt.
Create an editable settings screen with a profile, email alerts, and a Save button.

tools.name: PDF TO MP3 Canvas
tools.summary: Send text to a shared player for listening one sentence at a time.
use_when: Let the user listen to an answer.
Read source text or an explanation aloud.
Let the user read along and replay sentences.
not_for: Upload a PDF file directly to the text API.
inputs: text prepared from a PDF or document

access.auth: You do not need an account or plugin. Anyone can create a canvas. Later edits need the returned upload code.
requirements: Read the guide. Send JSON through HTTP requests.
For speech, the user enters a Gemini key in the player and presses Play.

limits: Anyone with the player link can read the text. The link gives no edit rights.
Canvases do not expire. Upload codes last 24 hours.
Never send a Gemini key to the Canvas API. The user enters it in the browser.
Speech, Ask, and Explain use the user's Gemini key.
Each canvas allows up to 500,000 source and spoken characters in total. Each request must fit within 1 MiB.
tools.example_prompt:
Read https://pdftomp3.com/canvas/guide.html.
Explain how memory works.
Send the text to PDF TO MP3 Canvas.
Open the player link that the tool returns.

tools.name: In-App Editor
tools.summary: Edit a copy of a website in the browser. Copy a prompt to apply the edits to its files.
use_when: Add an editor to an existing website project.
Move, resize, or add items on a copy of a page.
Give an agent a prompt that describes the user's visual edits.
not_for: Apply edits to website files without an agent.
Build and host a website from a design brief.
outputs: prompt for edits to website files

access.auth: The editor runs in the browser. It needs no separate account or server.
requirements: Access to the website project files.
Copy in-app-editor.js and LICENSE into the website project. Include index.js if the app uses imports.
Load the editor once in the browser after the page is ready.
Show the EDIT button in local builds and private previews only.

limits: The editor changes a separate page copy. An agent must apply the change prompt to the website files.
Keep draft storage off. Each edit session must start from the current page.
The page copy does not run the page's scripts.
The editor cannot copy content inside frames or closed shadow roots.
Video, custom components, and complex transforms can differ in the copy.
The change prompt describes the visual result. Apply the edits through the website's layout rules. Check wide and narrow screens.
tools.example_prompt:
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/janpmz/in-app-editor/main/instructions.md.
Add In-App Editor from https://github.com/janpmz/in-app-editor to this website.
Show the EDIT button in local builds and private previews only.
